q: What is a Personal AI Operating System?
options: Software you install on your computer
Your day designed — the same AI moments at the same times
A folder of AI tools you use occasionally
A backup system for your files
explanation: A computer without an OS is parts, and you without a routine are the same. The system is your day, designed: the same AI moments at the same times, so the gains compound instead of scattering.

q: Which approach matches the lesson's guidance for building your system?
options: Adopt all five blocks exactly as described
Pick the two or three blocks that fit your job and write them down
Use AI whenever you remember to
Skip the weekly review to save time
explanation: You do not need all five blocks — you need the ones that fit your job, written down, because an unwritten system does not survive Mondays. For each block note the tool, trigger, prompt or workflow, and output.

q: What is the purpose of the weekly review?
options: To add more automations every week
To see what the system saved you, what you skipped and what output was useless, then adjust one thing
To replace all your tools with new ones
To measure how much time you spend on AI
explanation: Once a week, spend fifteen minutes asking what the system saved you, what you skipped and what output was useless, then adjust one thing. Systems that get reviewed get better; systems that don't get abandoned.
